transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Dr. Linh Tran (HelioGenomics ML Lead), Marcus Cole (Infra), Priya Nair (Product)

Auto-generated summary (brief, may be imperfect):
- Reviewed latest pilot bench runs comparing Redwood runtime vs incumbent baseline (OrbisAI).
- Identified p95 latency regression on long-context prompt (5k tokens) attributed to KV cache population and a routing misconfig on customer side.
- Agreed on tuning steps: adjust batching window, pin quantized model variant for mid-tier traffic, increase cache pre-warm for prefix-heavy prompts, and fallback policy thresholds.
- Next steps: Redwood to share raw traces and pricing delta; HelioGenomics to run steadystate test against dedicated slot.

Topics: Results review, latency/throughput deltas, cache hits, batching, quantization tradeoffs, fallback playbooks, security handoffs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay, um, thanks everyone for joining. we have about, what, 55, 58 minutes. quick agenda: results recap, tuning proposals, fallback rules and next steps. Owen, do you want to start with the headline numbers?
[00:23] Owen: yeah sure. so, quick TLDR. in our mixed prompt suite (prod-like mix, 60% short, 40% long) overall token throughput, um, improved versus Orbis by about 22% in terms of tokens/sec when using our continuous batching and prefix cache. p50 latency for short calls is roughly comparable, 90-120 ms, both systems. the delta shows up in p95 on long-context prompts — we measured p95 of 820 ms on Redwood vs 640 ms on Orbis for the 5k token-ish traces. caveat: those runs had different warm-start conditions.
[01:12] Dr. Linh: can i ask, is that with the quantized variant? like the 4-bit quantized model we agreed to test?
[01:21] Owen: yes that's with our q4-ish profile, but we also had some runs with the float16 baseline. interestingly, the quantized variant gives lower avg cost but the p95 tail widened a bit when the KV cache miss rate was high. the cache hit-rate in those runs dropped to around 52% for long prefix sequences; when we pre-warmed the cache the p95 came down to about 710 ms.
[01:48] Marcus: wait, so are we seeing miss because of routing or because the test harness didn't keep persistent connections? we— we have ephemeral clients in our harness.
[01:58] Owen: yep, so two factors. one is the harness session behavior, the other is our routing: some of the requests were accidentally routed to a different model variant during a canary that ran mid-day. that would flush K-V in memory or cause a miss if the instance wasn't warmed.
[02:17] Priya: that's the thing we flagged last week, the canary toggle in our infra toggled overnight — sorry, mornings — and that might have created the mismatch.
[02:28] Dr. Linh: hmm okay. so to validate, we need a steady-state run with pinned variant and with connections kept alive for at least, like, five minutes to simulate real app behavior.
[02:38] Maya: agreed. we can help with a wrapper to keep sockets warm, and we'll also share a script to pre-warm the KV cache with the top 200 prefixes from your prompt corpus.
[02:49] Marcus: that would help. also, are we certain the latency tail is due to KV and not to batching window settings? we noticed some micro-bursts in the client which could cause larger batch waits.
[03:02] Owen: good point. we saw a correlation: when the batching window was bumped to 30 ms to favor throughput, the p50 improved but the p95 for large generations increased because large generations sometimes queued up behind smaller quick requests — increasing head-of-line wait time. so there's a tradeoff: lower per-token cost vs tail latency.
[03:25] Dr. Linh: so what's the recommended config for our use-case? our SLA target is p95 < 750 ms for the large prompts and overall cost per 1M tokens should not exceed $1200.
[03:37] Owen: for that SLA, recommendation is: pin quantized model for mid traffic, set batching window to 20 ms, enable prefix KV pre-warm for top 200 prefixes, and route any overflow above 80 rps to a lower-cost float16 model variant with a per-request fallback threshold at 900 ms. that keeps p95 under 750 in the lab for most runs.
[03:57] Priya: i want to check that math on cost. if we route overflow to float16, what's the unit cost impact?
[04:04] Maya: we'll put the rough delta in the pricing sheet but ballpark is about 8-12% higher in commit cost if you keep steady dedicated slots; though on pay-as-you-go hosted it's about 18% cheaper than Orbis for our q4 runs due to batching efficiency. we'll send the numbers.
[04:20] Dr. Linh: unrelated security note — we need to validate KMS integration and ensure logs have immutable audit entries. Marcus, are you ready to do the security sync?
[04:31] Marcus: yes, i'll need your security SME on that. i also want to confirm retention windows because their defaults differ from ours.
[04:38] Maya: yep, we'll bring our security SME next week. we have SOC2 docs and KMS flow diagrams.
[04:45] [05:00] Owen: another anomaly i want to call out — on the 3/12 run we saw a spike where p95 shot to 1.4s for about 40 seconds. tracing shows a routing hop to a node with a different kernel selection; that was due to autoscaler spin-up and a transient model-variant mismatch. so we added a small cooldown to autoscaler and pinned model slots during the test; that removed the spike.
[05:28] Dr. Linh: do you have the trace? can we share that?
[05:33] Owen: yes, i'll include the raw trace and a short writeup. note that the trace labels are a bit noisy in the export — sometimes kernel names appear truncated as, um, "kern-alu-32" or as "k-al-32" in the tool.
[05:45] Priya: are there any functional regressions vs Orbis? we saw some slight prompt formatting differences in output in a couple of samples last week.
[05:56] Maya: nothing systemic in scoring — those were mostly tokenizer quirks. we included normalization and detokenization steps but it's worth running a small eval harness. we can run a tokenized diff and highlight samples.
[06:10] Dr. Linh: ok. for the steady-state run, we want: pinned variant, persistent connections, 15-20 ms batching window, KV pre-warm, and 30-minute run at 70 rps; then we'll compare p50/p95 and unit cost against Orbis baseline.
[06:25] Owen: sounds good. one more thing — fallback thresholds. we propose two-tier fallback: first try model_variant_A (q4 pin), if response not streaming within 700 ms then route to model_variant_B (float16 lower-cost); if still not served within 900 ms return precomputed cached answer for top-20 intents. this reduces user-facing timeouts.
[06:45] Marcus: do you have a playbook for that? if we switch mid-conversation we need to preserve context.
[06:52] Owen: yep, the playbook includes preserving KV prefix and re-hydrating the prompt; the session id and partial tokens are stitched so the downstream sees a coherent exchange. caveat: stitching can add ~40-60 ms overhead.
[07:06] Priya: that's acceptable if it keeps UX intact. can we simulate stitching overhead in the lab?
[07:11] Owen: yes, we can include that in the next run. we'll add a stitching payload to the harness.
[07:18] Dr. Linh: awesome. security again — Marcus will need the KMS key import docs.
[07:24] Maya: i'll attach the KMS integration guide and the SOC2 audit summary.
[07:28] [07:45] Owen: quick note — competitor mention: Orbis does slightly better at cold-start p95 on raw float16 due to their larger instance pool, but their cost per token is ~20% higher in our modeling for the production-like mix. CloudPrompt came up in the procurement thread but we haven't run head-to-head.
[08:05] Dr. Linh: okay. anything else on routing?
[08:10] Maya: one ask — Marcus, can you try the dedicated slot we've provisioned for you for a short run on Wed 3/18? we'll stand by to collect logs.
[08:18] Marcus: yes, i can. i'll coordinate with infra and do a 30-minute steady-state at 70 rps as discussed.
[08:24] Maya: perfect. last section: recap of decisions and owners.
[08:28] Owen: recap: 1) Redwood to share raw traces, trimmed latency spreadsheet, and pre-warm script. 2) HelioGenomics to run pinned-variant steady-state test on 3/18. 3) Security sync scheduled for 3/20. 4) Maya to send pricing delta.
[08:43] Priya: and we'll validate outputs with our product e2e tests once we have the results.
[08:47] Dr. Linh: thanks everyone.
[08:50] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts. bye.
